parsed.why: No criminalisation and police work with the LGBTI group, but no trans-specific protections, undefined social acceptance, undated LGBT assaults, official insensitivity, and a 2017 legal analysis warning mismatched passports could draw charges. Elevated risk.

Gender identity covered by hate-speech and anti-discrimination law since 2013/2020, recourse operating (Pride shooter got maximum 30 years), liberal climate, hostile attitudes falling; negatives are rising reports and poor clearance. Low risk.

State-imposed universal exposure: documents forced to birth sex, X markers stopped, passports confiscated, entry refusal and lifetime-ineligibility risk, facility bans, harmful custody, counterterrorism naming pro-trans groups. Near bottom.

Gender-imitation offence struck down in 2022, but enforced morality and same-sex laws used against LGBTQ people, documented official discrimination against trans people persisting, enforced dress codes, no document change, no recourse.

Strong formal trans framework and no criminalisation, but 2025 care-ban decrees, prison-housing decree, abolished anti-discrimination agency, gender-motivated aggravator unapplied, record aggregated hate-crime year. Reduced risk, deteriorating.
